entry.title: The popular scientific course started today!

link.title: The popular scientific course started today!

entry.content: The evening course on Fungal Biology (Svamparnas biologi) given at SU started today. We had 32 fungal enthusiasts in the group, wanting to learn all there is to know about fungi. We have also launched the open homepage that will be used as a resource in this course and that can also be used by other interested. See the course webpage here: https://svamparnasbiologi.org/

entry.title: Ivar leaves the group.
entry.content: Today, we said farewell to Ivar, who leaves the group. Thanks Ivar for the productive and dedicated years in our group. And good luck with the next steps in your career! We will miss you!

entry.title: Otto Orrvik starts in the group.

link.title: Otto Orrvik starts in the group.

entry.content: Otto joins the group for a master thesis on the invasive bolete Aureoboletus. Otto aims to solve the dispersal and reproductive biology of the bolete as it has invaded Europe. Very exciting! We look forward to seeing the outcome.

entry.title: Sten Svantesson starts in the group.

link.title: Sten Svantesson starts in the group.

entry.content: Today Sten Svantesson starts in the group. As one of Sweden’s few fungal systematists, specializing in basidiomycetes, he will be an asset to the group, as we more and more focus our research on that phylum! Welcome Sten!

entry.title: Welcome Jean-Loup!
entry.content: Today, Jean-Loup starts as a postdoc in the group. He will work on TEs of the mosaic genomes of Verticillium longisporum. Great to have you joining the team!

entry.title: Boel’s manuscript accepted in Royal Society Open Science

link.title: Boel’s manuscript accepted in Royal Society Open Science

entry.content: Boel got her manuscript on the growth of fairy rings accepted for publication in the journal Royal Society Open Science. In this paper, we perform a transplant experiment to disentangle the reasons behind the peculiar growth of the fairy rings. Will be in print soon!

entry.title: Rosa leaves the lab
entry.content: We had a nice fika to say farewell to Rosa, who leaves us after having been with us for a little more than a year for her master-thesis! We have learned so much on the fairy-ring microbiome and other things, have enjoyed the time together a lot. Now, we wish her the best of luck in the future!

entry.title: End of the semester
entry.content: The group celebrated the end of the semester and went to the Natural History Museum next door for a guided tour, getting to see many interesting drawings and collections of plants and fungi. Thanks for hosting us, and especially to Sten and Mia for the guiding!
